title: Plantation and jute workers
author: Editorial Desk
summary: Two old industries, two BMS federations, and the questions of wages and housing.
body:
BMS has a federation for each of two traditional industries: the **Bharatiya Plantation Mazdoor Mahasangh** and the **Bharatiya Jute Mazdoor Mahasangh**.

## Plantation workers

Tea, coffee, rubber and spice plantations in Assam, West Bengal, Kerala, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu employ lakhs of workers, many of them women and many belonging to families that have lived on estates for generations. The **Plantations Labour Act, 1951** gave them housing, medical care and education for children. The OSH Code now contains many of its provisions.

Plantation workers' common issues include **wages** that are fixed through tripartite or State committees, **housing quality**, **land rights** for estate residents and the closure of **sick gardens**.

## Jute workers

The jute industry is concentrated in West Bengal. Mills employ large workforces; many are on contract. Issues include **wage agreements**, closure and reopening of mills, raw jute prices and the Jute Packaging Materials Act, which requires use of jute bags for certain commodities.

## Common concern

In both industries the question is whether an old industry can be modernised without throwing its workers out. BMS argues that modernisation and employment must go together.
